findings.title: Migration crashes when the legacy embed_category setting was never persisted
findings.body: The migration unconditionally indexes the first row returned by the `embed_category` query (`...[0]['id']`). Site settings with their default value are not necessarily stored in `site_settings`, so a deployment that configured allowed hosts but left the category at its default has no `embed_category` row. In that common case `[0]` is nil and the migration aborts before it can fall back to Uncategorized. Handle an empty result before indexing it (and likewise make the fallback query robust).

findings.title: Legacy hosts are copied without normalization and stop matching requests
findings.body: The old setting accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/path` (the existing tests explicitly cover those forms), but this migration inserts those strings verbatim. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` subsequently extracts only the request hostname and compares it to the stored `host`, so a migrated row containing a scheme or path can never authorize that host. Existing embedding installations using those supported legacy formats will begin rejecting embeds and topic retrievals after migration. Normalize each legacy value to its hostname before inserting it.

findings.title: Duplicate host mappings make the destination category nondeterministic
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database unique index on `host`, while the admin UI/API permits creating multiple rows for the same host. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no ordering and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that record's category, so duplicate entries for one hostname can route imported posts to an arbitrary category depending on database query order. Enforce a case-insensitive unique host constraint (and clean/deduplicate migration input) so each hostname has one unambiguous mapping.

findings.title: Updates and deletes of nonexistent hosts raise 500 errors
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `where(...).first` and immediately call `save_host` or `destroy` without checking whether a row was found. A stale admin page or request for an unknown ID therefore raises `NoMethodError` instead of returning a normal 404/not-found response. Use `find`/`find_by!` or explicitly render a not-found error before dereferencing the record.
